questions.q: Which condition, also known as icterus, causes a yellowing of your skin and the whites of your eyes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is jaundice Key Points

• Jaundice (Icterus) is a condition where the skin, the whites of the eyes (sclera), and sometimes other tissues develop a yellow tint.

• This yellowing happens because of an excessive buildup of a substance called bilirubin in the blood.

• Bilirubin is a yellow pigment produced during the normal breakdown of red blood cells.

• Normally, the liver processes bilirubin and excretes it into bile, which helps digest fats.

• The bile is then eliminated from the body through stool.

• Causes of Jaundice

• Pre-hepatic (before the liver):

• Caused by increased destruction of red blood cells (hemolysis).

• Examples: Sickle cell anaemia, malaria.

• Hepatic (in the liver):

• Caused by liver diseases that impair its ability to process bilirubin.

• Examples: Hepatitis, cirrhosis, alcoholic liver disease.

• Post-hepatic (after the liver):

• Caused by an obstruction in bile ducts that prevents bilirubin from being excreted.

• Examples: Gallstones, tumors, bile duct strictures.

Additional Information

• Ichthyosis

• Ichthyosis refers to a group of skin disorders that cause dry, scaly, and thickened skin, resembling fish scales.

• It is a chronic condition, often genetic, though it can sometimes occur due to other health issues (acquired ichthyosis).

• Eczema

• Eczema (also known as atopic dermatitis) is a chronic inflammatory skin condition that causes red, itchy, and inflamed patches on the skin.

• It’s commonly triggered by allergens, irritants, or stress.

• Pemphigus

• Pemphigus is a rare autoimmune disorder that causes painful blisters on the skin and mucous membranes (such as the mouth, throat, and genitals).

• The body’s immune system mistakenly attacks the proteins that hold skin cells together.

questions.q: Which of the following celebrations is dedicated to Sun God and his wife Usha to thank them for sustaining life on earth and for granting wishes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Chhath Puja Key Points

• Chhath is predominantly a Hindu festival dedicated to the Sun god and his wife Usha with the motive of thanking them for providing the bounties of life on the Earth.

• The literal meaning of the word chhath is sixth and hence, this festival is celebrated on the sixth day of the Kartika month of the Hindu calendar "Vikram Samvat".

• The festival has a duration of four days. The rituals under this festival include a holy bath, keeping the fast, remaining in water for long periods of time, along with offering prayers and food to the setting sun and the rising sun.

• The main worshipers are known as Parvaitin,(usually women). Although, it's seen that sometimes men also observe this festival as it is essentially not a gender-specific festival.

• The festival is observed primarily in Mithila Province of Nepal, Terai-Madhesh region of Nepal along with the Indian states of Bihar, Jharkhand, and UP.

• Moreover, it is also observed in areas where migrants from the above-mentioned areas have their presence.

Additional Information

• Madai Festival

• The Madai Festival is celebrated primarily by the Gond tribes of Madhya Pradesh and is a significant cultural event that showcases their rich traditions and heritage.

• It typically involves vibrant rituals, traditional dance forms, music, and communal feasting, reflecting the community's connection to nature and agriculture.

• The festival usually marks the harvesting season and is a time for the tribes to give thanks for the bounty received.

• Vishwakarma Puja

• Vishwakarma Puja is dedicated to Lord Vishwakarma, the divine architect and craftsman of the universe, celebrated by artisans, builders, and craftsmen across India.

• This festival often includes the worship of tools, machinery, and vehicles, symbolizing the reverence for craftsmanship and engineering skills.

• The Puja is marked by colorful decorations, offerings, and cultural performances, emphasizing creativity and innovation in various trades.

• Sorath Sabha

• Sorath Sabha refers to a cultural and social gathering primarily associated with the Rajput community, particularly in the Sorath region of Gujarat.

• These gatherings promote community bonding, sharing of cultural traditions, and discussions on social issues, fostering a sense of unity among members.

• The Sabha often features traditional music, dance, and storytelling, highlighting the rich history and heritage of the Rajput community.

questions.q: What is the relationship between interest rate and demand for money?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Inverse Key Points

• Interest rates bear an inverse relationship with the demand for money.

• Opportunity costs of holding money will be high when interest rates are high;

• people are losing out on possible earnings that interest-bearing investments could have generated.

• When interest rates are high, the opportunity cost of holding money increases because people can earn more by investing their money rather than keeping it as cash.

• This leads to a lower demand for money for transactional and speculative purposes

• When interest rates are low, the opportunity cost of holding money is low.

• People prefer holding more money for transactions or precautionary needs because the benefit of investing it is minimal.

• This leads to a higher demand for money.

• The relationship can be visualized using the liquidity preference theory by John Maynard Keynes:

• The demand for money (liquidity preference) decreases as the interest rate increases, and vice versa.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution explains that the executive power of every state shall be so exercised as not to impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union, and the executive power of the union shall extend to the giving of such directions to a state as may appear to the Government of India to be necessary for that purpose?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Article 257 Key Points

• Article 257 of the Constitution of India explains that the executive power of every state shall be exercised in a way that does not impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union

• Article 257(1) of the Constitution of India states that the executive power of every state shall be exercised in a way that does not impede or prejudice the exercise of the executive power of the Union.

• This article is essential to ensure that the Union and the states exercise their executive power in a harmonious manner.

• It also enforces the principle of Union supremacy by giving appropriate directions in the event of irreconcilable differences on vital issues.

• Article 257 shapes the relationship between the center and states in India, addressing the principle of federalism

Additional Information

• Article 261 (Public acts, records, and judicial proceedings)

• It ensures that full faith and credit shall be given throughout the territory of India to public acts, records, and judicial proceedings of the Union and states.

Judicial Process:

• The law defines how acts, records, and judgments will be authenticated and proved for recognition across state borders.

• Article 247 (Power of Parliament to provide for the establishment of certain additional courts)

• It grants the Parliament the authority to establish additional courts for better administration of laws made by it regarding matters listed in the Union List.

questions.q: Madhav purchased an item for ₹42,000 and sold it at a loss of 20%. With remaining amount, he purchased another item and sold it at a gain of 30%. What is the overall gain (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Successive percentage change formula: Net % Change = x + y + (x × y)/100

⇒ Net % Change = −20 + 30 + (−20 × 30)/100

⇒ Net % Change = 10 − 6 = +4% (Overall Gain)

⇒ Overall Gain = 4% of ₹42,000 = (4/100) × 42000 = ₹1680

∴ The correct answer is ₹1680.

Alternate Method



Given:

Initial Cost Price = ₹42,000

Loss on the first sale = 20%

Gain on the second sale = 30%

Calculations:

⇒ Selling Price of first item = 42000 × (100 − 20)/100

⇒ Selling Price of first item = 42000 × 0.80 = ₹33,600

⇒ Since the new item is bought with the remaining amount, New Cost Price = ₹33,600

⇒ Selling Price of second item = 33600 × (100 + 30)/100

⇒ Selling Price of second item = 33600 × 1.30 = ₹43,680

⇒ Overall Gain = Final Selling Price − Initial Cost Price

⇒ Overall Gain = 43680 − 42000 = ₹1680

∴ The correct answer is ₹1680.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is sequentially changed by a% and then by b%, the net percentage change is given by: Net % = a + b + (a × b)/100. Use a positive sign for gains/increments and a negative sign for losses/decrements.

Base Value in Profit and Loss

In any business transaction, profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the initial Cost Price (CP) unless explicitly stated otherwise.

Multiplying Factor Method

To directly calculate the final amount after multiple percent changes, use multiplying factors. Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± x/100) × (1 ± y/100).

questions.q: What is the volume (in cm³) of a cylinder if the radius of the cylinder is 8 cm and the height is 14 cm? (Take 𝝿 = 22/7)
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Since the volume formula uses π (22 ÷ 7), the final answer must be a multiple of 11.

We check the given options using the divisibility rule for 11 (difference of sums of alternating digits):

Option 1: 2686 → (6 + 2) − (8 + 6) = 8 − 14 = −6 (No)

Option 2: 2816 → (6 + 8) − (1 + 2) = 14 − 3 = 11 (Yes)

Since only 2816 is exactly divisible by 11, it is the correct volume.

∴ The correct answer is 2816 cm³.

Alternate Method

Given:

Radius of cylinder (r) = 8 cm

Height of cylinder (h) = 14 cm

Formula Used:

Volume of cylinder = π × r² × h



Calculation:

⇒ Volume = (22 ÷ 7) × 8² × 14

⇒ Volume = 22 × 64 × (14 ÷ 7)

⇒ Volume = 22 × 64 × 2

⇒ Volume = 44 × 64

⇒ Volume = 2816 cm³

∴ The correct answer is 2816 cm³.

Additional Information

Curved Surface Area of Cylinder

The curved surface area is calculated as 2 × π × r × h, representing the outer lateral surface.

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The total surface area includes the top and bottom circular bases, calculated as 2 × π × r × (r + h).

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same base radius and height has exactly one-third the volume of the cylinder: (1 ÷ 3) × π × r² × h.

questions.q: Seven years ago, Prachi was four times as old as her daughter was at that time. Four years from now, Prachi will be two-and-a-half times as old as her daughter would then be. Find the sum of the present ages (in years) of Prachi and her daughter.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Ratio of ages (Prachi : Daughter) 7 years ago = 4 : 1 (Difference = 3 parts)

Ratio of ages 4 years from now = 2.5 : 1 = 5 : 2 (Difference = 3 parts)

Since differences are equal, 1 ratio part = Total time gap = 7 + 4 = 11 years.

Sum of ages 7 years ago = 4 + 1 = 5 parts = 5 × 11 = 55 years.

Sum of present ages = 55 + (7 × 2) = 69 years.

∴ The correct answer is 69 years.

Alternate Method

Given:

Let Prachi's present age be P and her daughter's present age be D.



Calculations:

⇒ Seven years ago: P − 7 = 4 × (D − 7)

⇒ P − 4D = −28 + 7

⇒ P − 4D = −21 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ Four years from now: P + 4 = 2.5 × (D + 4)

⇒ P − 2.5D = 10 − 4

⇒ P − 2.5D = 6 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Subtracting Equation 1 from Equation 2:

⇒ (P − 2.5D) − (P − 4D) = 6 − (−21)

⇒ 1.5D = 27

⇒ D = 18 years

⇒ Substitute D = 18 in Equation 1:

⇒ P − 4 × 18 = −21

⇒ P − 72 = −21 ⇒ P = 51 years

⇒ Sum of present ages = P + D = 51 + 18 = 69 years

∴ The correct answer is 69 years.

Additional Information

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two individuals remains constant at any point in time. This is a fundamental concept used to balance ratio parts in age-related problems.

Sum of Ages Shift

If the sum of present ages of n people is S, then t years ago, their sum was S − nt, and t years later, it will be S + nt.

Ratio Balancing Method

If the difference between two quantities is unchanged, multiply the ratios by suitable integers to make the difference in ratio parts equal. Then each ratio part can be directly equated to the real-world value.

questions.q: The marked price of an article is 26% more than its cost price. If a discount of 32% is given, what will be the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

We can use the successive percentage change formula: Net Change % = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, Markup (a) = +26% and Discount (b) = −32%

Net Change = 26 − 32 + (26 × −32) ÷ 100

∴ The correct answer is 14.32%.

Alternate Method

Given:

Markup percentage = 26%

Discount percentage = 32%



Formula Used:

MP = CP × (1 + Markup% ÷ 100)

SP = MP × (1 − Discount% ÷ 100)

Loss% = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100

Calculations:

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) = 100

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 26 = 126

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 126 × (1 − 32 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 126 × 0.68

⇒ SP = 85.68

⇒ Loss = CP − SP = 100 − 85.68 = 14.32

⇒ Loss % = (14.32 ÷ 100) × 100 = 14.32%

∴ The correct answer is 14.32%.

Additional Information

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is sequentially changed by a% and then by b%, the net percentage change is given by the formula: Net % = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Markup and Discount Relation

The final Profit or Loss percentage is simply the successive application of the Markup percentage and the Discount percentage. Using the successive formula: Profit/Loss % = Markup% − Discount% − (Markup% × Discount%) ÷ 100.

Selling Price Link

The Selling Price acts as a bridge between the Cost Price and Marked Price. SP = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss)% and SP = MP × (100 − Discount)%.

Shortcut Trick

Using the algebraic difference of cubes identity: x³ − y³ = (x − y)(x² + y² + xy)

Substitute x = sinA and y = cosA into the given expression directly:

⇒ [(sinA − cosA)(sin²A + cos²A + sinA × cosA)] ÷ (sinA − cosA)

⇒ sin²A + cos²A + sinA × cosA

⇒ 1 + sinA cosA

∴ The correct answer is 1 + sinA cosA.

Alternate Method

Given:

Expression: (sin³A − cos³A) ÷ (sinA − cosA)

Formula Used:

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

sin²A + cos²A = 1

Calculation:

⇒ Expand the numerator using the difference of cubes formula.

⇒ Numerator = (sinA − cosA)(sin²A + cos²A + sinA × cosA)

⇒ Substitute this expansion back into the fraction:

⇒ [(sinA − cosA)(sin²A + cos²A + sinA × cosA)] ÷ (sinA − cosA)

⇒ The common term (sinA − cosA) cancels out from the numerator and the denominator.

⇒ We are left with: sin²A + cos²A + sinA × cosA

⇒ Applying the basic trigonometric identity sin²A + cos²A = 1.

⇒ 1 + sinA cosA

∴ The correct answer is 1 + sinA cosA.

Additional Information

Sum of Cubes Identity

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²). This is extremely useful for expressions like (sin³A + cos³A) ÷ (sinA + cosA) which easily simplifies to 1 − sinA cosA.

Basic Trigonometric Identities

1 + tan²A = sec²A and 1 + cot²A = cosec²A. These fundamental identities along with sin²A + cos²A = 1 are frequently used to simplify complex trigonometric fractions.

For algebraic or trigonometric simplifications where options are in terms of functions, substituting standard angles like A = 30° or 60° (avoiding values where the denominator becomes zero) can help quickly verify the correct option during exams.

questions.q: Without doing the actual division, find the remainder when 28735429 is divided by 9.
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

To find the remainder when a number is divided by 9, apply the casting out nines technique.

Cancel out any digits or groups of digits in 28735429 that sum to 9.

Cancel 9, the pair (2 + 7), and the pair (5 + 4).

The remaining digits are 8, 3, and 2.

Sum of remaining digits = 8 + 3 + 2 = 13 ⇒ 1 + 3 = 4.

∴ The correct answer is 4.

Alternate Method

Given:

Number = 28735429

Divisor = 9

Method Used:

The remainder of a number divided by 9 is the same as the remainder of the sum of its digits divided by 9.

Calculations:

⇒ Sum of digits = 2 + 8 + 7 + 3 + 5 + 4 + 2 + 9

⇒ Sum of digits = 40

⇒ Divide 40 by 9: 40 = 9 × 4 + 4

⇒ The remainder obtained is 4.

⇒ Alternatively, the sum of digits of 40 = 4 + 0 = 4.

∴ The correct answer is 4.

Additional Information

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is completely divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3. The remainder obtained is the same as dividing the sum of digits by 3.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is 0 or a multiple of 11.

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is exactly divisible by 8.

Digital Root Concept

The single-digit value obtained by repeatedly summing the digits of a number is its digital root, which gives the exact remainder when the number is divided by 9.

questions.q: At present, A is thrice as old as B. C is 5 years elder than B. The sum of the ages of A, B, C is 75 years. The ratio of the age of B five years ago to the age of A three years from now is:
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Let B's present age be x.

Then A = 3x, and C = x + 5.

Total sum: 3x + x + x + 5 = 75 ⇒ 5x = 70 ⇒ x = 14.

Present ages: B = 14 years, A = 3 × 14 = 42 years.

Ratio of (B − 5) to (A + 3) = (14 − 5) : (42 + 3) = 9 : 45 = 1 : 5.

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 5.

Alternate Method

Given:

A is thrice as old as B ⇒ A = 3B

C is 5 years elder than B ⇒ C = B + 5

Sum of ages of A, B, and C = 75 years

Formula Used:

Past age = Present age − Number of years

Future age = Present age + Number of years



Calculations:

Let the present age of B be x.

⇒ Present age of A = 3x

⇒ Present age of C = x + 5

According to the given condition, sum of their ages is 75:

⇒ 3x + x + (x + 5) = 75

⇒ 5x + 5 = 75

⇒ 5x = 70

⇒ x = 14

Now, calculate the required ages:

⇒ Present age of B = 14 years

⇒ Present age of A = 3 × 14 = 42 years

⇒ Age of B five years ago = 14 − 5 = 9 years

⇒ Age of A three years from now = 42 + 3 = 45 years

Find the required ratio:

⇒ Required Ratio = 9 : 45

⇒ Required Ratio = 1 : 5

∴ The correct answer is 1 : 5.

Additional Information

Past and Future Ages

If the present age is x, then age n years ago is (x − n) and age n years from now is (x + n).

Constant Difference

The difference between the ages of two persons always remains constant irrespective of past, present, or future times.

Ratio of Ages

If the ratio of present ages of A and B is a : b, then their actual ages can be assumed as ax and bx respectively, where x is a common constant multiplier.

questions.q: The average temperature of a city for the first sixteen days of January is 22ºC, and the average temperature for the last sixteen days of the same month is 26ºC. If the average temperature for the entire month is 24ºC, what is the temperature on the sixteenth day?
questions.solution:
Shortcut Trick

Average temperature of 31 days in January = 24ºC

Total deviation for first 16 days = 16 × (22 − 24) = −32

Total deviation for last 16 days = 16 × (26 − 24) = +32

Net deviation = −32 + 32 = 0

Temperature on the 16th day = Average + Net Deviation = 24 + 0 = 24ºC

∴ The correct answer is 24ºC.

Alternate Method

Given:

Average temperature of first 16 days = 22ºC

Average temperature of last 16 days = 26ºC

Average temperature of the entire month (31 days) = 24ºC

Formula Used:

Temperature of overlapped day = (Sum of part 1) + (Sum of part 2) − (Total sum)

First 16 days: 22ºC

Last 16 days: 26ºC

Calculations:

⇒ Sum of temperatures of first 16 days = 16 × 22 = 352

⇒ Sum of temperatures of last 16 days = 16 × 26 = 416

⇒ Total sum of temperatures for the entire month = 31 × 24 = 744

⇒ Temperature on the 16th day = (352 + 416) − 744

⇒ Temperature on the 16th day = 768 − 744 = 24

∴ The correct answer is 24ºC.

Additional Information

Arithmetic Mean (Average)

The average is the sum of all values divided by the total number of values. Formula: Average = Sum ÷ Count.

Overlapping Groups Principle

When two subsets overlap on a single item (like the middle day in a month), the value of the overlapping item is determined by adding the sum of both subsets and subtracting the total sum of all items.

Deviation Method

The sum of total deviations from the exact average is always zero. This property can be used as a smart shortcut to quickly find missing or overlapping values by balancing the positive and negative net deviations against the base average.
